attempts.label: DANDI:001868
attempts.entry_title: Learning-induced plasticity of ICMS responses in mouse S1 (Kim, Lycke et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's main behavioural and electrophysiology findings largely held up in this data. Thresholds fell with learning (median 5.39 to 3.88 uA), and modulation rose over training in pyramidal and pulse-locked units but not in non-pulse-locked units. Population coupling rose in pulse-locked units. Several findings did not hold: pulse-locking identity was stable across currents in only 79% of unit-channel pairs (the paper says over 80%), and the hit-miss separation (KL divergence) and the hit-miss divergence onsets did not match. All imaging findings (activation density and radius, tracked neurons) could not be tested, because the files lack stimulation-contact positions in the imaging volume and any identity of a cell across sessions. The same gap blocks the waveform and unit-tracking findings, since each unit has only one mean waveform. Conduction velocity at 4 uA fell just below the expected range.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Lycke, Zolotavin, Montes, Xie and Luan (2026) on dandiset 001868, which holds chronic electrophysiology, wheel behaviour and two-photon imaging of mouse S1 during an intracortical microstimulation detection task. It tests the behavioural thresholds, response times and movement onset, the modulation and pulse-locking of sorted units over training, their hit-miss separation and population coupling. The imaging claims are blocked, as the files lack the stimulation-site position in the imaging volume, the activation calls and the identity of planar ROIs across sessions.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Kim, Lycke et al. (2026) from dandiset 001868

outcomes.notes: psignifit thresholds at the default grid (the current at 50% of the fitted function, mean of block thresholds per channel and session, weeks 0 to 4, six mice) have medians of 5.39 uA early (n = 46) and 3.88 uA late (n = 89), both within tolerance (late 3.78 to 4.62), and late is lower (two-sided Mann-Whitney p = 5.32e-06, r = 0.39; paper p = 7.68e-6, r = 0.40). The early n is within 43 +- 4; the late n of 89 is one above 80 +- 8, an expected value the criterion does not judge. psignifit's unscaled threshold gives 5.41 and 3.84 uA. The bounded maximum likelihood variant, not the criterion's fit, gives late medians of 3.71 (mu) and 3.70 uA (x50), below the tolerance, with p = 4.9e-07 and 5.15e-06. Without Mouse 6, 5.17 and 3.91 uA (p = 7.61e-05). Every mouse is lower late.
deviations: Thresholds are refitted with psignifit 4.3 (Python), sigmoid norm, yes/no, at psignifit's default grid. The threshold is the current at which the fitted (scaled) function reaches 0.5, as the criterion says and as the paper's code takes it (processing/dataloader.py, get_block_detection_threshold, ps.getThreshold(result, 0.5), XieLuanLab/icms-activation-plasticity at d1922d1). The paper's code calls an older psignifit. The dataset stores no thresholds.

Blocks are the 100-trial groups of the volumetric trials; the planar fifth block is left out as the Methods count four blocks (Methods, Analysis of behavioral data). 38 channel-sessions have two blocks and 4 have one or three.
Mouse 6 (ICMS83) has no catch trials in its files, so its fits have no 0 uA point.

outcomes.notes: Median psignifit threshold per week is 6.495, 4.658, 3.866, 4.310 and 3.808 uA for weeks 0 to 4. The fall from week 0 to 1 (1.837 uA) is larger than each later change (largest 0.792 uA, week 1 to 2). psignifit's unscaled threshold gives 1.775 against 0.846 uA. The maximum likelihood variant, which is not the criterion's fit, reverses the order (mu 1.016 against 1.186 uA, x50 1.139 against 1.257 uA, week 1 to 2).
deviations: The criterion's reading of Fig. 2A (week medians) is the claims file's assumption.
Thresholds as in fig2a-threshold-decrease (psignifit, default grid, 50% of the fitted function).

outcomes.notes: Median over mice of the per-mouse median hit response time at 4 to 6 uA is 274.9 ms in week 0, 199.2 in week 1 and 193.9 over the late phase; 93% of the fall (75.7 of 81.0 ms) is between weeks 0 and 1. From the train onset, 265.4 and 186.8 ms (93%). Variant, hit trials early against late, 190.1 against 173.8 ms, p = 7.19e-17, r = -0.14.
deviations: The dataset's response_time is from trial start, which precedes the train onset by 5.5 to 37 ms in most sessions, 0 in Mouse 6 and 56 to 85 ms in ICMS101 2023-10-27; the time from train onset is shown as a variant and gives the same result.
Currents 4 to 6 uA, as the common method of the claims file fixes.

outcomes.notes: Per-animal thresholds (11.8 to 14.5 a.u.) give median onsets of 119.0 ms in Mouse 1, 133.0 ms over all hit trials and 128.0 ms in the late phase, all within tolerance; early 144.0 ms (n = 1307) against late 128.0 ms (n = 2897), p = 6.09e-32, r = -0.23 (paper n 1305 and 2922, r = -0.22). The pooled threshold gives 118.0, 134.0 and 129.0 ms and p = 1.94e-29. The 568 of 4772 hit trials with no onset are the 568 with no stored wheel trace; every hit trial with a trace has an onset.
deviations: The paper takes the response threshold from hit and miss trials; the dataset's miss trials have no response time except 98, so the threshold is taken from hit trials, with those 98 added as a variant (same thresholds).
The stored wheel_position_processed is already low-passed at 20 Hz forward and backward (its description), so no filter is applied again.
Onset is measured from the train onset of the electrical_stimulation table.

outcomes.notes: Weeks 0 to 4, reading (a) unit-sessions, 795 units (584 pyramidal, 204 interneurons, 7 unknown), 488 modulated (339 pyramidal, 146 interneurons). The modulated total and the modulated pyramidal count are within tolerance; the totals of all, pyramidal and interneuron units and the modulated interneurons are below it (2 of 6, the criterion asks 5). Over all 55 sessions, 999 units (732, 260) and 585 modulated (405, 177), 3 of 6. With the Methods filters alone the counts are the same. With the trough-to-peak rule on the stored mean waveform, 577 pyramidal and 218 interneurons, 334 and 154 modulated. Every unit is marked accepted. Reading (b) cannot be formed, as no unit identity across sessions is stored. The outcome rests on the counts, 4 of 6 outside their tolerance where the criterion asks 5 inside. The trough-to-peak histogram in 0.05 ms bins alternates (59, 22, 44 at 0.40 to 0.55 ms), but at 30 kHz a bin holds one or two possible values, and per value the counts are 29.5, 22 and 22, so the dip comes from the binning; no bimodality is judged.
deviations: Cell type is the stored cell_type, which the files describe as the putative cell type from t2p classification; Mouse 6 spells it 'Pyramidal Cell' and 'Narrow Interneuron', read as the same labels. By the trough-to-peak of the stored single-channel mean waveform, 72 units change class (shown as a variant).

outcomes.notes: Time to maximum falls at 5 uA (80 to 45 ms, p = 0.00522, r = -0.12) and not significantly at 6 uA (105 to 75 ms, p = 0.168), but also falls at 4 uA (75 to 55 ms, p = 0.0465, r = -0.09; paper p = 0.18), so the absence at 4 uA does not hold.

Reading (a), channel-session medians at the current nearest the psignifit session threshold, early 3.93 (n = 42) against late 3.30 (n = 87), p = 0.16, r = -0.15. Reading (b), every response at that current, p = 0.789. With the maximum likelihood x50 threshold, p = 0.702. The n of (a) are twice the paper's 21 and 34; the criterion names (a) as the reading whose n matches, and it does not match here (asked in questions/001868.yaml).

Mouse 1 at 4 uA, modulated responses per channel and session, early median 12 (n = 8) against late 14 (n = 21), one-sided p = 0.0443, r = 0.42, as in the paper (n 8 and 21, p = 0.044, r = 0.42). All six mice, p = 0.0728, not significant, as the paper says. Mice 5 and 6 alone give p = 0.00232 and 0.0165.

Pyramidal z rises at 4, 5 and 6 uA (p = 4.79e-05, 0.000587, 0.000878; r = 0.23, 0.18, 0.20) and time to maximum falls at 5 uA (65 to 25 ms, p = 0.000329, r = -0.18) and 6 uA (85 to 35 ms, p = 0.025, r = -0.13). It also falls at 4 uA (p = 0.0208), where the paper reports p = 0.32. The code's one-sided tests halve these p. With cell types from the trough-to-peak rule on the stored mean waveform (variant), z rises at all three currents (p = 0.000212, 0.000435, 0.000492) and time to maximum falls at 5 uA (p = 0.000362) but not at 6 uA (p = 0.0587).

outcomes.notes: Interneuron z does not change (p = 0.331, 0.884, 0.0885; r = 0.08, -0.01, 0.15; n 55/221, 90/158, 90/76 against the paper's 69/254, 113/180, 122/86). 740 unit-channel pairs with modulated responses at two or more of 4 to 6 uA; 389 all PL, 197 all NPL, 49 NPL to PL, 89 PL to NPL, 16 mixed; fraction keeping identity 0.792 (0.72 to 0.908 by mouse), below the 0.80 the claim states. With three other seeds of the PL call, 0.774, 0.793 and 0.789.

The density half cannot be formed: the control survey files hold ROI masks and binary activation per channel and current, with contact positions in um, but no voxel size or plane spacing (the imaging plane has no grid_spacing; its description gives 51 to 171 planes), and 2 to 9 of the 32 contact positions are at the origin with no stated mapping from Ripple channel to contact index. The count half was run on the stored activation calls (all activated ROIs, as the 800 um limit cannot be applied): at 5 uA the count falls from a median of 10 early to 2 late, channel x session p = 0.0146 (late weeks 2 and 3) and 0.00573 (weeks 2 to 4), channel x week medians p = 0.0816 and 0.0261 (n 63 early, 43 to 67 late; paper p = 0.066, n 42 and 26), so it gives P >= 0.05 under one of four combinations. The files hold 24 control imaging sessions where the paper reports 18; the controls were imaged at 2, 5, 7 and 10 uA.

The planar ROIs are segmented in each session (385, 172, 388, 359, 697, 329, 543 and 443 ROIs in Mouse 1), their roi_id_source is the row index 0 to N-1 in every session, so the files carry no identity of an ROI across sessions, and no mean or reference images are stored (reference_images is empty in every planar and volumetric segmentation), so the PatchWarp alignment and mask matching of the Methods cannot be repeated. The ROI description says only that the planar ROIs are a separate segmentation from the volumetric one. Every Fig. 3 and fig. S6 claim rests on tracked neurons.

The units table holds one mean waveform per unit (90 samples on one channel); there are no waveforms of spikes in and out of stimulation and no multi-channel waveforms for the PCA.
UnitMatch needs each unit's multi-channel template; the files hold one single-channel mean waveform per unit and no labels of tracked units.

Reading (a), 5 uA (the code's current): 111 modulated control responses in 14 sessions of 4 mice, PL 32 early and 19 late, NPL 27 and 33 (paper 29/12 and 30/29). PL modulation p = 0.946 (r = -0.01), NPL modulation p = 0.122 (r = 0.23), PL time to maximum p = 0.112 (r = 0.25), NPL time to maximum p = 0.399 (r = 0.13), PL peak spike probability p = 0.182 (r = -0.23); none is significant. Reading (b), all currents pooled (n 59/73 PL, 74/103 NPL, further from the paper's), gives NPL modulation p = 0.00809 and PL time to maximum p = 0.0352. The criterion judges under the reading whose n is closest to the paper's, (a). The bursts of a trial start 0.5 s apart, so the 700 ms baseline holds an earlier burst for 5863 of 8795 bursts. With every burst's baseline taken from the 700 ms before its trial's first burst (variant, same PL labels), NPL modulation rises (0.334 to 0.988, p = 0.0059, r = 0.43, n 29 and 28) and the other four tests give p = 0.744, 0.957, 0.44 and 0.07. The absence of a change in NPL modulation therefore holds with the code's baseline and not with a baseline free of stimulation; the claim of absence is judged on the code's test as followed, and the variant is reported. PL time to maximum rises here (5 to 55 ms, r = 0.25), where the paper reports r = -0.39.
deviations: Control units follow the paper's control code (processing/control/postprocessing/create_session_responses.py and process_control_responses.py, python/fig_s7/generate_figure.py, XieLuanLab/icms-activation-plasticity at d1922d1): each 200 ms burst is a train, the baseline is the 700 ms before it, stimulation spikes are the unblanked ones in 20 ms pulse windows, pulse-locking uses 20 ms windows, filters P < 0.05, z > 0, baseline at least 0.5 Hz, more than 5 trains, more than 15 pulse-window spikes, weeks below 5, 5 uA; weeks from each animal's first ephys session, the first dates the code lists (python/utils/config.py). The code's timing file (control_timing_params.json) is not in the repository: the 20 ms window comes from the code's docstring, the 1.5 and 0.5 ms blanking is the behavioural one, and time to maximum is taken over the burst. These are assumptions.
The controls were stimulated at 2, 5, 7 and 10 uA, so reading (b) pools all four currents.

The 700 ms baseline before each burst holds the previous burst for the second and third burst of a trial (5863 of 8795 bursts). A baseline from the 700 ms before the trial's first burst is run as a variant; whether the code's missing timing file sets another baseline is asked of the authors (findings).

findings.statement: The behavioural files give no position of the stimulation contacts in the volumetric imaging volume (the electrode table gives positions along the probe only) and no activation calls, and they hold per-ROI dF/F, not the voxel-level responses the activation rule uses. The paper's counts, densities and radii of activated neurons (Fig. 2B to 2G, fig. S2) cannot be formed.

Planar ROIs are segmented separately in each session and carry no identity across sessions, and no mean or reference images are stored for alignment, so the neurons tracked across weeks in Fig. 3 and fig. S6 cannot be found.

Each unit has one mean waveform of 90 samples on one channel. Waveforms of spikes in and out of stimulation (Fig. 4D) and the multi-channel templates UnitMatch needs (fig. S8) are not in the files, nor are labels of the tracked units.

The Methods say the control animals had similar stimulation parameters to the behavioural group, but the control files describe and hold 3 bursts of 10 biphasic pulses at 50 Hz per trial (200 ms bursts starting 0.5 s apart), where the behavioural trains are 70 pulses at 100 Hz over 700 ms.

The control survey imaging gives no voxel size or plane spacing, and 2 to 9 of its 32 stimulation contact positions sit at the origin with no stated mapping from Ripple channel number to contact index, so distances of ROIs from the stimulation site cannot be formed.

The files hold 795 unit-sessions in the 46 sessions of weeks 0 to 4 (999 over all 55 behavioural sessions), where the paper reports 973 units; 24 control imaging sessions where the paper reports 18; and units in 14 sessions of 4 control mice where fig. S7 reports 4 animals and 15 sessions.

The trials table gives no response time for miss trials except 98, so the movement-onset threshold of fig. S5 (25th percentile over hit and miss trials) cannot be formed as stated; and response_time is measured from trial start, which precedes the train onset by 0 to 85 ms depending on the session (56 to 85 ms in ICMS101 2023-10-27).
Mouse 6 (ICMS83) has no catch trials in its files (currents 2 to 10 uA only), though the Methods give each block 10 catch trials; its thresholds cannot use the false-alarm point.

The electrical_stimulation tables describe 700 ms, 70-pulse trains, but in sessions with planar imaging they also hold 37 to 90 trains of up to 242 pulses lasting seconds, after the end of the electrophysiology recording.

Cell types are spelled 'Pyramidal Cell', 'Narrow Interneuron' and 'unknown' in ICMS83 and 'pyramidal' and 'interneuron' elsewhere; and the stored type disagrees with the 0.45 ms trough-to-peak rule applied to the stored mean waveform for 72 units (29 interneurons at 0.45 ms or more, 43 pyramidal below).

Question for the authors (fig. 6D). What bin width and smoothing were used for the hit and miss PSTHs, and was the divergence onset the first significant cluster or the last? With 10 or 5 ms bins and no smoothing, PL responses show significant clusters in both phases and the early NPL onset (first cluster) is 75 ms with 10 ms bins and 87.5 ms with 5 ms bins.

Question for the authors (fig. S5, E to H). Were the modulated set and the PL labels recomputed in the 120 ms window or kept from the 700 ms analysis? Kept, the NPL modulation does not change; recomputed, it rises at all three currents.

stim_channel and the electrode table's channel_name are both described as Ripple channel numbers, but they are not the same numbering. The paper's code places stimulation channel c at (32 - c) x 60 um on the probe; with that the contacts lie at 0 to 520 um depth and, pooled over mice, the fraction of modulated units falls with distance from them (not in Mice 5 and 6, nor in the nearest 60 um), while taking the electrode table's rel_y for channel_name = c puts them at -156 to 1559 um, some outside the electrode table, and shows no fall-off pooled. The mapping from stim_channel to a contact position is not stated in the files.

No per-pulse stimulation times are stored; the trains have onsets and offsets only (every behavioural train lasts 700.00 ms), so pulse-locked analyses must place the pulses at their nominal 10 ms (20 ms in the controls) spacing.

Question for the authors (fig. S7, fig. S9C). The control code reads control_timing_params.json and condensed_trials.csv, which are not in the repository. Were the pulse window 20 ms and the blanking 1.5 and 0.5 ms, and was time to maximum taken over the burst, and was the baseline the 700 ms before each burst, which holds the previous burst? With a baseline before each trial's first burst, control NPL modulation rises (p = 0.0059). Is a row of condensed_trials.csv a trial of 3 bursts or one burst? With trial rows the control PL and NPL coupling do not differ (FDR p = 0.431 and 0.134); with burst rows they differ early (FDR p = 0.00428).

In the control files the trials table's trial_index is described as the trial index within the session, but it restarts in each recording block (rep_num), so the same index names up to several trials of a session, and the electrical_stimulation table's trial_index, which refers to it, cannot tell them apart without the block.

The verifier queried the archive's file list and metadata and tested the helper on synthetic inputs. Report in transcripts/001868/verifier-1-report.md.

disagreements.reason: Cell 19: 795 units, 584 pyramidal, 204 interneurons, 488 modulated (339 pyramidal, 146 interneurons). Only 2 of 6 counts are within tolerance (modulated, modulated pyramidal); the all-55-sessions variant gets 3 of 6. Cell type comes from the stored cell_type, not from the criterion's trough-to-peak rule (the two disagree for 72 of 795 units).
Cell 23: the 5 uA test holds (p = 0.0052), but 4 uA is also significant (p = 0.0465). The criterion requires P >= 0.05 there.

Cell 35, stored labels: PL 0.747 and NPL 0.536 are both within tolerance, Fisher p = 4.9e-5. Under the criterion's own cell-type rule (trough-to-peak, the variant), NPL is 0.582, outside 0.448 to 0.548.
Cell 43: 6 uA holds (p = 0.036), but 5 uA does not (p = 0.86).

Cell 55: in the 120 ms window NPL > PL in both phases (FDR p = 2e-7 and 1e-12). The control half is blocked (methods_underspecified): the control ephys exists but the trains differ; modulation and time to maximum over the 200 ms bursts could have been tested under a stated assumption.

entries.name: 001868-kim-2026
entries.title: Learning-induced plasticity of ICMS responses in mouse S1 (Kim, Lycke et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kim, Lycke, Zolotavin, Montes, Xie and Luan (2026) on dandiset 001868, which holds chronic electrophysiology, wheel behaviour and two-photon imaging of mouse S1 during an intracortical microstimulation detection task. It tests the behavioural thresholds, response times and movement onset, the modulation and pulse-locking of sorted units over training, their hit-miss separation and population coupling. The imaging claims are blocked, as the files lack the stimulation-site position in the imaging volume, the activation calls and the identity of planar ROIs across sessions.
